newsitem.title: USA: Florida judge holds arena ruling until after vote.
newsitem.headline: Florida judge holds arena ruling until after vote.

text.p: A Florida judge said Friday he would withhold his ruling on the validity of Dade County's arena bond referendum until after the polls close on Nov 5.
Dade County Court Judge Ronald Friedman also said he would rule next week on whether the ballots should be counted immediately, or sealed pending resolution of litigation.

"He was concerned about the validity of the electoral process," said county Elections Supervisor David Leahy. "Regardless of which way he rules it may be appealed. It makes it difficult to conduct an election when you don't know whether the question is on or off the ballot."
Dade County has agreed to issue $165 million of revenue bonds through the Miami Sports Authority to build a new basketball arena for the Miami Heat on public park land adjacent to the Port of Miami.
Debt service on the arena bonds would be paid from an existing hotel tax, arena revenues and a sales tax rebate.
Attorney Dan Paul and his political action committee, the Stop the New Arena Committee, gathered enough petition signatures to put the bond proposal on the Nov 5 ballot.
The group objects to both the use of tax money and the use of public land for the arena, which would be the second built for the Heat in seven years.

The Heat filed suit on Sept 25 seeking to have measure stricken from the ballot on grounds that it is confusing, misleading and addresses several issues, in volation of a local law restricting referendums to a single topic.
Friedland heard arguments in the case Friday, but said he would not release his ruling until 2000 EST on Nov 5, an hour after the polls close.
